Update SWIFT_VERSION from 5.0 to 6.0 in all 4 places in project.pbxproj (lines 882, 914, 931, 949)

userStories.title: Remove UIKit appearance proxies for Liquid Glass
userStories.description: As a user, I want the app to use iOS 26 Liquid Glass design on tab bars and navigation bars.
acceptanceCriteria: Wrap the entire body of configureAppAppearance() in BookiApp.swift (lines 62-90) with `if #unavailable(iOS 26) { ... }` so it only runs on iOS 18-25
On iOS 26, tab bar renders with system Liquid Glass translucency (no opaque override)
On iOS 26, navigation bar renders with system Liquid Glass translucency
Tab bar tint color still uses Theme.accent via SwiftUI .tint() modifier on TabView
On iOS 18, the existing opaque dark appearance is preserved (guard ensures old code runs)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: BookiApp.swift has configureAppAppearance() called in init(). The method sets UITabBar.appearance() and UINavigationBar.appearance() with opaque backgrounds. Wrapping in #unavailable(iOS 26) means the opaque overrides only apply on older iOS. On iOS 26, the system Liquid Glass applies automatically. The .tint(Theme.accent) on TabView in ContentView.swift handles selected tab color natively.

userStories.title: Update tab badge styling for Liquid Glass
userStories.description: As a user, I want tab badges to remain legible on the Liquid Glass tab bar.
acceptanceCriteria: Wrap the UITabBarItem badge appearance code in ContentView.init() with `if #unavailable(iOS 26) { ... }`
On iOS 26, badges use system default styling (which works with Liquid Glass)
On iOS 18, badges still use brand teal (Theme.accent) background with dark text in SpaceGrotesk-Bold
Picks tab badge still shows open bet count (1-9+)
Members tab badge still shows flagged player count
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: ContentView.init() has UITabBarItem.appearance().badgeColor and setBadgeTextAttributes calls. These UIKit overrides may conflict with Liquid Glass. Guard them with #unavailable(iOS 26). The .badge() SwiftUI modifier on the tab items works independently of the UIKit appearance.

userStories.title: Migrate AuthManager to @Observable
userStories.description: As a developer, I want AuthManager to use @Observable for better performance and modern patterns.
acceptanceCriteria: AuthManager class uses @Observable macro instead of ObservableObject protocol
All 10 @Published properties become plain var properties (remove @Published)
BookiApp.swift changes @StateObject var authManager to @State var authManager
BookiApp.swift changes .environmentObject(authManager) to .environment(authManager)
All views using @EnvironmentObject var authManager updated to @Environment(AuthManager.self) var authManager
Auth flow works: login, logout, role detection, bookie/player routing
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes:
AuthManager is used in ~15 files via @EnvironmentObject. The migration pattern:
1. AuthManager.swift: Replace `class AuthManager: ObservableObject` with `@Observable class AuthManager`. Remove all `@Published` from properties.
2. BookiApp.swift: `@StateObject private var authManager` → `@State private var authManager`. `.environmentObject(authManager)` → `.environment(authManager)`.
3. Every view with `@EnvironmentObject private var authManager: AuthManager` → `@Environment(AuthManager.self) private var authManager`.
Files with @EnvironmentObject authManager: ContentView, AuthGateView, SettingsView, DashboardView, PlayersListView, PlayerMainView, AccountView, LoginView, SignUpView, ForgotPasswordView, OnboardingContainerView, OnboardingProfileView, PlayerClaimView, AnalyticsDashboardView, and PlayerSettingsContent in ContentView.

userStories.title: Enable strict concurrency and fix warnings
userStories.description: As a developer, I want strict concurrency checking enabled so the app is safe under Swift 6.
acceptanceCriteria: Add SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = complete to build settings in project.pbxproj
All @Observable service classes have @MainActor annotation where appropriate
Fix Sendable conformance warnings on types passed across isolation boundaries
Fix any nonisolated async function warnings (Swift 6.2 changed behavior — they now inherit caller's isolation)
Edge function calls, sync operations, and bet submission still work correctly
Zero concurrency warnings in build output
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes:
This is the hardest story. Swift 6 enforces strict data isolation. Key areas to check:
- BetSlipManager and FavoritesManager need @MainActor (they access UI state)
- EdgeFunctionService.callFunction() is async — in Swift 6.2, nonisolated async functions run on caller's actor. If called from @MainActor view, network calls could block main thread. May need @concurrent annotation.
- SyncService async methods may need similar treatment.
- UserDefaults access must happen on MainActor.
- Combine usage patterns with sink/assign may need Sendable closures.
Start by adding the build setting, then fix warnings file by file.
